Entering data types: text, numbers, dates
Formulas beginning with = and built-in functions (SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT, IF at a naming level)
Cell references and the relative vs absolute distinction; $ locks a reference when copying

claims.claim: A spreadsheet is a grid of cells where columns are lettered and rows numbered, and a cell's address (cell reference) combines its column letter and row number, e.g., B3.
A cell can hold text, a number, or a date, and the program treats these types differently; numeric functions ignore values stored as text.

A formula begins with an equals sign, and its result is displayed in the cell while the formula stays in the formula bar; functions such as SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT, and IF perform common calculations, and =SUM(B2:B6) adds a range.
By default cell references are relative and adjust automatically when a formula is copied; copying =SUM(A1:A9) into the adjacent right column produces =SUM(B1:B9).

An absolute reference is written with dollar signs before the column letter and row number (e.g., $A$1 or $A$1:$B$2) and stays fixed when a formula is copied; references may also be mixed ($A1, A$1), and the F4 key cycles a reference through these forms.
Spreadsheets can present data as dynamic charts that update automatically when the data changes, and can sort, filter/hide ranges, and compute subtotals.

In the worked example, =SUM(B2:B6) over 1200, 850, 430, 610, 300 equals 3390 and =AVERAGE equals 678; copying =B2*$E$1 (with E1=0.08) down yields 96, 68, 34.40, 48.80, and 24 because $E$1 stays locked while B2 advances.

sourceRecords.title: Addresses and References, Absolute and Relative (LibreOffice Calc Help)
sourceRecords.notes: Official LibreOffice Calc documentation, read via WebFetch on 2026-08-19. Supports: by default references are relative and adjust automatically when copied; copying =SUM(A1:A9) into the adjacent right column produces =SUM(B1:B9); absolute references use dollar signs formatted as $A$1:$B$2 and stay fixed when copied; the F4 key cycles a reference through $A$1, A$1, $A1 and back to relative. Used to verify reference behavior and the copy example underpinning the worked example. Reference-only; no wording reproduced in the lesson.

sourceRecords.title: LibreOffice Calc Features (Help overview)
sourceRecords.notes: Official LibreOffice Calc feature overview, read via WebFetch on 2026-08-19. Supports: Calc provides functions (including statistical and banking functions) used to build formulas for calculations; a Function Wizard assists formula creation; dynamic charts update automatically when data changes; users can reorganize the sheet to show or hide data ranges and quickly calculate subtotals and totals. Used for the functions, charts, and sorting/filtering claims. Reference-only; no wording reproduced.
